summary: Sylvain Lévi (1863–1935) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the Sorbonne under Abel Bergaigne and held chairs at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and Collège de France.

Sylvie Hureau works in sinology and Buddhist studies. She has held posts as maître de conférences at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (attested 2012) and as a Research Fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Sze-bong Tso is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He completed his PhD at the Australian National University (1977–1982), where he studied under doctoral supervisors Jan Willem de Jong and Tissa Rajapatirana.

Sándor Kőrösi Csoma (1784–1842) was a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at Bethlen Gábor College, the University of Göttingen, and with traditional teachers Sangye Phuntsok and Kunga Cholek Dorje, later serving as Librarian at The Asiatic Society.
Søren Sørensen (1848–1902) was an Indology scholar. He held teaching posts at the Herlufsholm School from 1876 to 1878 and at the University of Copenhagen from circa 1887 until 1902.
Sāmaṇera Bodhesako (1939–1988) worked in Buddhist studies. He founded Path Press and served as an editor at the Buddhist Publication Society.
Sīlaratano studied under Narada Maha Thera, Ajahn Maha Bua, and Nyanaponika Thera.

T. A. Gopinatha Rao (1872–1919) worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He served as Tamil Assistant at the Archaeological Survey of India (c. 1905–1908) and Superintendent of Archæology for the Travancore State (c. 1908–1919).

T. Chandrasekharan was an Indologist who studied under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He served as Professor of History of Sanskrit Language and Literature at Madras Sanskrit College (attested 1951), where he succeeded T. R. Chintamani.

T. Ganapati Sastri (1860–1926) was an Indologist who earned a Doctor of Philosophy from the University of Tübingen (c. 1924). He served as Curator of the Oriental Research Institute and Manuscripts Library and Editor of the Trivandrum Sanskrit Series (c. 1908–1925).

T. Griffith Foulk specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan under Luis Oscar Gómez, taught at Michigan (c. 1987–1995), and served as Riggs Professor of Religion at Sarah Lawrence College.

T. K. V. Desikachar (1938–2016) worked in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied under Tirumalai Krishnamacharya from circa 1961 to 1989 and founded the Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram in 1976.

T. N. Ramachandran (1901–1973) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as an archaeologist at the Government Museum, Chennai (c. 1925–1934) and as curator of archaeology at the National Museum, New Delhi.

T. R. Chintamani was an Indologist who earned his PhD at the University of Madras studying under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He served as Librarian at Adyar Library and Research Centre and became Senior Lecturer in Sanskrit at Madras in 1933.

T. R. V. Murti (1902–1986) was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned a D.Litt. at Banaras Hindu University under Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, later directing its Centre for Advanced Study in Philosophy and teaching at Oxford and McMaster.
T. S. Devadoss is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who held academic posts at the University of Madras, including serving as Professor (attested 1994, 2008).

T. S. Eliot (1888–1965) studied at Harvard, Paris, and Merton College, working under George Santayana and Charles Rockwell Lanman. He held academic posts at Birkbeck, University of London (c. 1916–1919) and the University of Chicago (c. 1950).

T. S. Rukmani is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. She held positions at Miranda House (attested 1983–1989) and served as Chairperson of Hindu Studies in the Department of Religion at Concordia University (attested 1989).

T. S. Srinivasa Sastri was an Indology and philosophy scholar affiliated with Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, serving as Professor (attested 1984–1992, with affiliations attested in 1972 and 2007).
T. Shrinivas Shastri is an Indology scholar who held positions at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, including Pandit (attested 1993) and Professor (attested 2026).
